docs.title: ISO 20022 Address Schema
docs.text:
Financial messaging standard for transaction data. Source: generated standards page (ISO 20022 tab).

ISO 20022 defines a standardised, structured data format for financial messaging, including specific, granular fields for address components, primarily for efficiency and accuracy in financial transactions.

[!warning] Important ISO 20022 currently only applies to 32 countries.

docs.title: International Addressing Standards — Overview
docs.text: Comparison of UPU S42 and ISO 20022 for global address management. Source: generated standards page.

docs.title: UPU S42 — Postal Addressing
docs.text:
• Scope: Global postal addressing standard
  • Focus: Logical structure of postal addresses for mail delivery
  • Application: Postal operations and cross-border mail
  • Flexibility: Adaptable by any country

docs.title: ISO 20022 — Financial Messaging
docs.text:
• Scope: Financial transaction data format
  • Focus: Structured data for financial transactions
  • Application: Banking, payments, regulatory compliance
  • Coverage: Only 32 countries

docs.title: Key Differences
docs.text: Aspect UPU S42 ISO 20022 Type Postal addressing standard Financial messaging standard Structure Generic elements + country templates Highly structured XML tags Adaptability Flexible, country-specific Rigid, fixed format Best For Web applications, mail delivery Financial operations, compliance

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: UPU S42 is the better choice for most address management scenarios due to its flexibility and wider country coverage. See UPU S42 and ISO 20022.

docs.title: POC Address Application Design
docs.text: This note describes the current Address proof of concept, as published on the documentation page. The implementation uses the same browser-native approach as the Asset POC: static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, without a frontend framework or build system.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Browser["Static browser app<br/>HTML + CSS + JavaScript"]
    UI["Address UI<br/>search + results + details"]
    Client["Loqate client<br/>loqate-client.js"]
    Proxy["FastAPI proxy<br/>api/main.py"]
    Storage[("Browser localStorage<br/>API key + theme")]
    Leaflet["Leaflet map<br/>CDN library"]
    Loqate["Loqate Find + Verify APIs"]
    Tiles["OpenStreetMap tile service"]

    Browser --> UI
    UI --> Client
    UI --> Storage
    Client -->|HTTP API request| Proxy
    Proxy -->|HTTPS request| Loqate
    UI --> Leaflet
    Leaflet -->|Map tile requests| Tiles

The app loads directly as a static page. The interface and application logic are in src/poc-address-app.html; the request helpers are in src/loqate-client.js; the Loqate proxy is implemented in api/main.py. Leaflet is loaded from unpkg.com and OpenStreetMap provides map tiles. There is no frontend framework runtime, database, or build step.

docs.title: Address lookup flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant App as Browser app
    participant Proxy as FastAPI proxy
    participant Store as localStorage
    participant Loqate as Loqate APIs
    participant Map as Leaflet + OpenStreetMap

    User->>App: Choose country and enter query
    App->>Store: Read saved API key
    alt No API key
        App->>App: Search built-in sample addresses
    else API key configured
        App->>Proxy: GET /api/addresses/search
        Proxy->>Loqate: Find address (recursive container drill-down)
        Loqate-->>Proxy: Address results
        Proxy-->>App: Address results
    end
    App->>Map: Plot markers where coordinates are available
    User->>Map: Click preview or expand button
    Map-->>User: Show full-size interactive map
    User->>App: Select result from list or map
    alt No API key
        App->>App: Load matching sample verification data
    else API key configured
        App->>Proxy: POST /api/addresses/retrieve
        Proxy->>Loqate: Verify selected address and request geocoding
        Loqate-->>Proxy: Verified address fields
        Proxy-->>App: Verified address fields
    end
    App->>App: Format lines from AddressFormat and show fields
    App->>Map: Center map on verified coordinates when available

The supported country list is embedded in the page. Without a key, only the included sample searches (tf26rf and EC2M 7NH) return data. With a key, the browser sends the X-Loqate-Api-Key header to the FastAPI proxy, which calls Loqate. The API key field is in the search section.

The results map is a compact 165-pixel preview, like the Asset POC. Click the preview or expand button to open a full-size interactive map. Result markers can be selected from either view; the expanded map also supports panning and zooming.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Responsibility poc-address-app.html Static interface, styles, search and API key controls, map setup, sample responses, result selection, and address rendering loqate-client.js Calls the local FastAPI address endpoints for search and verification api/main.py FastAPI proxy for Loqate Find and Verify, including recursive Find container drill-down Leaflet Compact map preview, result markers, and expanded interactive map OpenStreetMap Map tiles and attribution for both map views Browser localStorage Stores the Loqate key under loqate_api_key and theme preference under poc-address.theme.v1

docs.title: Address formatting
docs.text: Loqate's AddressFormat value provides field names grouped into address lines with <BR> separators. The app splits the format into lines, resolves each field from the verification response, and displays non-empty values. When no format is supplied, it falls back to the response's Address field.

docs.title: Framework and runtime
docs.text: The application is plain browser-native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It has no package manifest, frontend framework runtime, or compile step. The FastAPI proxy exposes /health, /heartbeat, /api/addresses/search, and /api/addresses/retrieve; FastAPI publishes interactive documentation at /docs. The local Podman runner builds api/Containerfile, starts the proxy, and serves the browser client. GitHub Pages publishes the app as docs/index.html and the standards guide as docs/documentation.html.

docs.title: Security and limitations
docs.text:
• The Loqate API key is saved in browser localStorage and sent to the proxy in X-Loqate-Api-Key. This is not a production secret store.
  • The app and proxy have no authentication, cache, persistent address records, or user account.
  • Leaflet and OpenStreetMap require network access.
  • The built-in examples are fixed fixtures, not a local address database.
  • Map pins and geocodes do not prove postal deliverability, ownership, or legal status.

The documentation page's UPU S42 content is explanatory; the app delegates live address formatting and verification to Loqate rather than implementing a separate standard engine.

docs.title: UPU S42 Addressing Standard
docs.text:
Universal Postal Union framework for postal addressing. Source: generated standards page (UPU S42 tab).

The UPU S42 standard provides a comprehensive framework for postal addressing, designed to accommodate the diverse formats used by different countries. It includes a generic list of address elements and country-specific templates to guide users in formatting addresses correctly for mail delivery.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Universal framework adaptable by any country
  • Generic list of address elements
  • Country-specific templates
  • Promotes efficient mail processing and data verification
  • Designed for easy adaptation by web applications

docs.title: Address application architecture
docs.text: The Address POC is a browser-native static application with an optional FastAPI proxy. The canonical architecture diagram is architecture.puml and uses the PlantUML ArchiMate library.

docs.title: Current architecture
docs.text:
• The browser hosts the user interface, address search, result selection, detail rendering, and Leaflet map.
  • loqate-client.js calls the Address proxy for search, verification, and the verified-address catalogue.
  • The FastAPI proxy calls Loqate Find and Verify, caches successful search and retrieve responses in process memory, and stores successfully verified addresses in a process-local catalogue.
  • Cache entries are isolated by an API-key fingerprint and expire according to the configured TTL. Neither the cache nor catalogue is durable.
  • Browser localStorage stores the Loqate API key and theme preference; it is not a production secret store.
  • Leaflet requests map tiles from OpenStreetMap.

docs.title: Runtime boundaries
docs.text: The static browser app can run without the proxy using its built-in sample responses. Live Loqate search, verification, and catalogue retrieval require the FastAPI proxy and a caller-supplied Loqate API key. The proxy does not persist user accounts or address records.

docs.title: Asset — Product Requirements Document
docs.text: Status: draft for review. Owner: Solution Architecture. Updated: 2026-11-05.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Asset is a reusable record for a real-estate subject: land, an estate, a building, or a separately managed part of a building such as a house, apartment, office, or factory. An estate is a collection of land and buildings within a defined boundary. Assets can be related to describe how a larger property is composed, while each asset remains independently identifiable and reusable.

The product provides a consistent way for business processes to find, create, reference, and maintain real-estate records. It separates the identity and physical description of an asset from the parties, legal interests, matters, transactions, valuations, and work associated with it.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Property information is often captured differently in each transaction or business system. The same property can be duplicated under different addresses or descriptions, and a property record may ambiguously refer to a parcel, a building, a unit, or an entire estate. This makes it difficult to reuse data, understand what is included in a transaction, and maintain a reliable history.

The existing WIP model allows a WIP record to refer to a property, but a shared Asset definition is needed to clarify what that property represents and how it relates to other records.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Represent real-estate assets consistently across business processes.
  • Support land, sites/estates, buildings, and separately managed units.
  • Distinguish a property as a whole from its parcels, buildings, and units.
  • Give each asset a stable identifier and support external identifiers where available.
  • Reuse assets across instructions, matters, transactions, and reporting periods.
  • Record location and descriptive details without treating them as proof of legal title.
  • Preserve changes to asset details and relationships so historical records remain interpretable.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Replacing a land registry, cadastral system, property-management system, or GIS.
  • Establishing legal title, tenure, ownership, boundaries, or rights from descriptive data alone.
  • Managing the full lifecycle of a property transaction, instruction, or work-in- progress record.
  • Providing property valuation, pricing, investment advice, planning decisions, or legal advice.
  • Treating addresses as globally unique asset identifiers.
  • Requiring a single taxonomy to encode every country's legal property concepts.

docs.title: Users and responsibilities
docs.text: User Need Case handler / adviser Find or create the correct property and attach it to a matter or instruction. Operations Correct descriptions, identifiers, and component relationships with history. Property or asset specialist Understand the physical subject and the scope of a property record. Integrating systems Reference an Asset consistently without creating a local duplicate. Administrator / data steward Manage data quality, access, and source provenance.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Concept Meaning Asset A real-estate subject with a stable identifier, type, status, and descriptive details. Land parcel A geographically defined area of land. A parcel may exist without a building and may be linked to registry or cadastral identifiers. Estate A collection of land and buildings within a defined boundary. The estate is an asset in its own right and may be composed of separately identifiable land parcels and buildings. Its defined boundary describes the estate's scope; it does not, by itself, prove legal title, cadastral boundaries, or ownership. Site A location or operational grouping that may contain parcels, buildings, and units. A site is not necessarily an estate; use the estate classification when the defined-boundary collection is intended. Building A physical structure, such as a house, apartment building, office, or factory. Unit A separately identifiable or managed part of a building, such as an apartment, commercial area, or suite. A Unit records its enclosing Building; the Building exposes the related Units through the inverse of that same relationship. Asset relationship A typed relationship between assets, such as part_of, located_on, or associated_with, optionally effective-dated. It does not by itself establish title or legal boundaries. Party relationship A separately recorded relationship between an Asset and a Party, such as an ownership interest, lease, or management relationship. The relationship type and its evidence are explicit. Matter association A link from an Asset to a matter, instruction, or transaction with a context-specific role. It does not change the Asset's identity.

An apartment or commercial area within a building is recorded as a Unit and linked to its enclosing Building. The Building's list of Units is the inverse view of those links, not a separately maintained relationship. An estate has a defined boundary and may include multiple land parcels and buildings. The record should make its type, boundary representation, and known relationships clear.

docs.title: Find or create an Asset
docs.text:
1. A user or integrating system searches by known identifiers, address, name, or descriptive details.
  2. The system returns possible matches with their asset type and distinguishing information, subject to access permissions.
  3. The caller selects an existing Asset or creates one with a type and the minimum available details.
  4. The system assigns a stable identifier and records the source and creation event.

An uncertain match is presented for review; the system does not silently merge assets.

docs.title: Describe a larger property
docs.text:
1. The user identifies the relevant assets, such as a site, land parcel, building, and apartment unit.
  2. The user records explicit relationships between those assets.
  3. The user identifies whether each relationship is confirmed, reported, or unverified when source confidence is relevant.
  4. A matter can reference the appropriate level of asset without assuming that all related components are included.

docs.title: Associate a Party or matter
docs.text:
1. The user links a Party to an Asset with an explicit relationship type, or links the Asset to a matter with a context-specific role.
  2. Where applicable, the relationship includes effective dates, source, and evidence.
  3. Ending or correcting the relationship preserves its history and does not delete either the Party or the Asset.

docs.title: EuroWIP application — Property views
docs.text: The EuroWIP browser POC has two Property surfaces: an optional Property step in the New Instruction wizard and a read-only Property record view backed by kf_Property and the kf_DealProperty junction. These describe the current application surface, not the complete target Asset model in this PRD.

docs.title: Property step in New Instruction
docs.text:
• Property is an optional step between Client and Details. The user can continue without entering a property.
  • The step provides a country selector and address search. The user chooses a country before searching; at least three characters are required to run Find.
  • Search results are selectable; selecting a result invokes address verification and can populate Address, City, Postcode, Country, and coordinates in the form. The current form displays a Sector selector with Office, Residential, Retail, Industrial, and Other values.
  • Address fields can also be entered or corrected manually. Search and verification failures are shown in the UI; when verification fails after selecting a result, the search result's street text may still be filled and the user is told to check the remaining fields.
  • The Review step shows the address or "None". On Instruction creation, an entered address or city is resolved to a Property; the Instruction stores that Property as its primary property and copies the selected Sector to its own sector field.

docs.title: Current behavior
docs.text:
• The Properties list shows Property name, Sector, Site, the number of linked Instruction junction records, and the number of WIP lines that directly reference the Property.
  • List search matches Property name or Sector. It does not search Site or an independently stored address.
  • The Property detail header shows the Property name, Sector, and Site when present. Its detail fields are Property, Sector, and Site.
  • A Linked instructions (kf_DealProperty) subgrid shows each junction reference, Instruction reference, and Instruction status. Selecting a row opens that Instruction. When none are linked, the view displays an empty state.
  • The detail view provides navigation back to the Properties list. It does not provide Property create or edit actions.
  • The subgrid's Status column is the Instruction status, not the status of the kf_DealProperty relationship. The current query includes junction records without filtering by relationship status; the displayed count is therefore not an active-only count.

docs.title: POC data shape and gap to the Asset target
docs.text:
In the POC schema, kf_Property is represented by a required name, required Sector, and optional Site lookup. The Site record has a name. The kf_DealProperty junction links an Instruction and Property and includes relationship status (Active, Removed, or Sold), added/removed dates, and notes. The Property view does not display those junction details beyond the junction reference and linked Instruction.

The Instruction wizard can construct the Property name from address, city, postcode, and country. The current POC stores that combined value as the Property name, along with Sector; it does not persist separate address components, country, coordinates, Loqate verification ID or raw response, asset type, external identifiers, or a geospatial boundary on kf_Property. Coordinates and the verification response stay in wizard state. A Site is not automatically assigned by this flow.

The wizard sets the Instruction's direct property_id lookup. The Property detail subgrid, however, reads linked Instructions through kf_DealProperty. The current create flow does not create a kf_DealProperty row, so a wizard-created direct Property reference is not guaranteed to appear in the detail subgrid. The product must establish which relationship is canonical and keep creation, listing, and reporting consistent.

These are implementation observations, not a decision to remove the broader requirements above. In particular, address, geolocation, asset type, provenance, asset composition, and auditable Property maintenance remain target-model requirements or open design decisions. Confirm how the POC's Property and Site records map to the canonical Asset, Site, and Asset-relationship concepts before treating the current storage shape as the production schema.

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text: Priority: Must (required for MVP), Should (important but deferrable), Could (future enhancement).

docs.title: Asset identity and lifecycle
docs.text: ID Pri Requirement AST-1 Must Every Asset has a stable, unique identifier, an explicit asset type, an address, a geolocation, a display name or description, and a record status. AST-2 Must The system supports at least land parcel, site, estate, building, and unit classifications. AST-3 Must Asset type is not inferred solely from its address or matter role. AST-4 Must An Asset can be created, retrieved, searched, and updated by authorized users or systems. AST-5 Must Asset identity is independent from any Party, matter, instruction, transaction, or WIP record that references it. AST-6 Must A Party or matter can reference an Asset by its stable identifier. AST-7 Must An Asset can be marked inactive or archived without deleting historical references. Record status is distinct from planning, occupancy, ownership, or legal status. AST-8 Must Updates to an Asset do not silently rewrite previously recorded transaction or matter evidence. AST-9 Should Search supports identifiers, address/location, name/description, type, and status filters. AST-10 Should The system surfaces potential duplicates for review without automatically merging them. AST-11 Must An estate has a defined boundary represented by spatial geometry or a reference to an authoritative or recorded boundary definition, with source and capture date where known. AST-12 Must The estate boundary defines the scope of the estate record and must not be presented as proof of legal title, ownership, or cadastral parcel boundaries.

docs.title: Property details and location
docs.text: ID Pri Requirement DET-1 Must An Asset can hold a human-readable name and description in addition to its stable identifier. DET-2 Must Every Asset has an address describing its physical location. Store it as structured address fields where available; where no formal street address exists, capture an appropriate site/land description and country rather than inventing an address. DET-3 Must Every Asset has a geolocation. Store latitude and longitude with a declared coordinate reference system, source, capture date, and known precision or confidence. DET-4 Must External identifiers record their type, issuer or jurisdiction, value, and source where known. DET-5 Should The model supports separate postal, site, registered, or other address purposes where relevant, while identifying the primary physical address. DET-6 Should The model can store area or measurement values with an explicit quantity type and unit; conversion or aggregation must not discard the original unit or source. DET-7 Must Where an estate boundary is stored as geometry, record its coordinate reference system, source, capture date, and known precision or confidence. DET-8 Could Store geospatial boundaries for non-estate assets with a declared coordinate reference system, precision, source, and confidence. DET-9 Must The Property list and detail view expose the Property name, Sector, and optional Site association; the list also exposes linked Instruction and WIP reference counts. DET-10 Must The Property detail view lists Instructions through kf_DealProperty, shows the junction reference and Instruction status, and allows navigation to the selected Instruction. The displayed status must be identified as the Instruction status, not the junction status. DET-11 Must A Property with no linked Instructions displays an explicit empty state, and the detail view provides a route back to the Properties list. DET-12 Should Property search supports name and Sector at minimum; address and Site search are added when those values are modeled as distinct searchable fields. DET-13 Must The user interface distinguishes the kf_DealProperty relationship status and dates from the linked Instruction status. Relationship counts and subgrids must state whether they include removed or sold links. DET-14 Must The New Instruction flow provides an optional Property step with country, address, city, postcode, and Sector inputs; users can proceed without selecting a Property. DET-15 Should The Property step supports country-scoped address Find and Verify, presents selectable matches, shows verification errors, and permits review or correction of the returned fields. Unverified fallback values must not be presented as verified. DET-16 Must A Property selected or resolved in the New Instruction flow is represented through the approved canonical Instruction-Property relationship and is visible in the Property's linked-Instructions view. DET-17 Must Address, country, and coordinates are persisted as distinct location data with source and verification provenance; they are not collapsed into the Property display name.

docs.title: Asset composition and relationships
docs.text: ID Pri Requirement REL-1 Must The system can link assets using an explicit relationship type, such as part_of, located_on, or associated_with. REL-2 Must An Asset can have multiple related assets; the model must not assume every property is a simple single-parent tree. REL-3 Must Asset relationships can be ended without deleting their history. REL-4 Must Self-referential relationships and duplicate active links of the same type are rejected. REL-5 Must Relationship semantics do not imply legal ownership, title, boundary, or inclusion in a transaction unless explicitly represented and evidenced. REL-6 Should Users can navigate from an Asset to its related parcels, sites, buildings, and units, and inspect relationship dates and provenance. REL-7 Could Support complex shared boundaries, easements, and spatial intersections as explicit domain relationships or geometry, after requirements are agreed. REL-8 Must An apartment or commercial area modeled as a Unit must reference its enclosing Building through an explicit part_of relationship. For the effective period of that relationship, a Unit has one enclosing Building. REL-9 Must A Building exposes its Units by querying the inverse of the Unit-to-Building part_of relationship; the inverse must not be stored or edited as a separate link. REL-10 Must A Unit-to-Building relationship can be created, changed, or ended with validation and an audit event; changing the enclosing Building preserves the former relationship's history.

docs.title: Parties, matters, and evidence
docs.text: ID Pri Requirement ASSOC-1 Must A Party-to-Asset relationship has an explicit type and does not make the Party's relationship intrinsic or permanent. ASSOC-2 Must Ownership, leasehold, occupation, management, and other interests are distinct relationship types and must not be inferred from one another. ASSOC-3 Must A relationship may carry effective dates, source, and references to supporting evidence where applicable. ASSOC-4 Must Matter-specific roles, such as purchaser or seller, are recorded on the matter association, not on the Asset identity. ASSOC-5 Must The system does not assert legal title or ownership from an unverified user-entered association. ASSOC-6 Should A matter or instruction can reference multiple Assets and identify which one is primary, where the consuming process needs that distinction.

docs.title: Data quality, security, and audit
docs.text: ID Pri Requirement GOV-1 Must Every create, update, archive, and relationship change records actor, time, affected Asset, and change details. GOV-2 Must Where Asset details or relationships come from an external source, the source and capture time can be recorded. GOV-3 Must Access to non-public property or transaction information is authorized and auditable. GOV-4 Must Invalid asset types, malformed relationships, and unauthorized access return explicit errors. GOV-5 Must Asset data is retained, corrected, or anonymized according to the applicable records and data-protection policy. GOV-6 Should Data quality rules identify missing or conflicting key identifiers without treating absence as proof that an Asset is invalid.

docs.title: Data principles
docs.text:
• An Asset record identifies the subject; it is not the transaction, instruction, or financial WIP line.
  • A property description may refer to a parcel, site, building, unit, or combination. The selected type and relationships must make that scope visible.
  • An estate is a defined-boundary collection of land and buildings; its boundary is distinct from legal title and cadastral parcel boundaries.
  • An apartment or commercial Unit belongs to one enclosing Building at a time; the Building's related-Units view is derived from the Unit's part_of relationship.
  • An address is a location descriptor, not a unique identifier or proof of a boundary.
  • Every Asset has both an address (or a suitable site/land location description where no formal address exists) and a geolocation. The geolocation is a point identifying the Asset's location; an estate boundary is separate spatial data.
  • A larger property may contain multiple parcels or buildings; a unit may relate to a building without the relationship proving legal subdivision.
  • Asset composition is not necessarily a tree. The model must allow relationships without assuming exclusive parentage.
  • Ownership, tenure, occupation, management, and transaction roles are separate concepts and require explicit relationship types.
  • External identifiers and sourced facts retain their issuer, source, and provenance.
  • Do not infer legal or physical facts from names, addresses, or informal descriptions.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text: Measure Target Assets created with a stable identifier and explicit type 100% Matter or WIP references resolve to an Asset identifier 100% Asset and relationship changes with an attributable audit event 100% Unreviewed ambiguous Asset matches automatically merged 0 Historical matter records silently changed by Asset updates 0 Relationships interpreted as legal title without explicit evidence 0

docs.title: MVP scope
docs.text:
The MVP includes:

  • Stable Asset identity and explicit types for land parcel, site, estate, building, and unit.
  • Basic description, address, geolocation, external identifiers, and source metadata.
  • A defined boundary for estates, stored as geometry or a reference to a boundary definition, with provenance where known.
  • Search, retrieval, creation, and authorized update.
  • Explicit relationships between Asset records, including component relationships.
  • References from matters/instructions and typed Party-to-Asset associations.
  • Audit history, authorization, inactive/archive status, and validation.
  • The EuroWIP Property list and detail experience: Property name, Sector, optional Site, Instruction/WIP reference counts, and navigation to linked Instructions via kf_DealProperty.
  • The optional Property step in New Instruction, including country-scoped address search/verification, editable address fields, Sector selection, and association of the resulting Property with its Instruction.

The MVP does not require detailed GIS boundaries, automated registry integration, valuation, title verification, legal analysis, or a comprehensive international property taxonomy.

docs.title: Dependencies and open questions
docs.text:
1. Boundary representation: Which geometry format, coordinate reference systems, and authoritative boundary sources should be supported in the initial jurisdictions?
  2. Asset identity granularity: When should an apartment or other unit be its own Asset versus a detail of its building?
  3. Primary identifiers: Which land registry, cadastral, local-authority, or internal identifiers are required in each launch jurisdiction?
  4. Address and location: Which address standards, country codes, coordinate reference systems, and geospatial formats should be supported?
  5. Ownership and interests: Does the Asset service store Party relationships, or should a separate title/interest service own them and expose references?
  6. Evidence and provenance: Which sources are trusted for property attributes and relationships, and how should conflicting sources be resolved?
  7. Valuation and financial data: Should valuation be modeled separately, and which system owns valuation history?
  8. Tenancy and retention: What access, retention, correction, and anonymisation rules apply to asset and transaction-linked data?
  9. WIP integration: Confirm whether the existing WIP propertyId reference should point directly to the canonical Asset identifier or to an adapter/mapping.
  10. POC-to-target mapping: Is kf_Property the canonical Asset record, and how should its name/sector/site fields map to typed Assets and explicit Asset relationships?
  11. Property maintenance: Should the Property list/detail remain read-only, or should authorized users be able to create and update Property and Site records?
  12. Relationship display: Should the Linked Instructions subgrid show the kf_DealProperty status and dates, and should removed/sold links be included or separated from active Instruction links and counts?
  13. Address persistence: Should the address supplied in the Instruction wizard remain a display name, or be stored as structured Property address fields with geolocation and provenance?
  14. Instruction-Property consistency: Is the direct Instruction property_id lookup or kf_DealProperty the canonical association for the primary Property? Should the wizard create a junction record so the Property subgrid and counts reflect the association?

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• A user can create and retrieve an Asset of type land parcel, site, estate, building, or unit.
  • The Property list shows Property, Sector, Site, linked Instruction count, and WIP line count; searching by name or Sector returns matching records.
  • The New Instruction Property step can be skipped, or can use a country-scoped address search and verification; the user can inspect or correct the address and Sector before creating the Instruction.
  • When a Property is supplied during Instruction creation, the canonical Instruction-Property relationship is created and the Property detail view shows the linked Instruction.
  • Opening a Property shows its name, Sector, and optional Site, plus the kf_DealProperty-linked Instructions with their link reference and Instruction status. Selecting a linked Instruction opens that record.
  • A Property with no linked Instructions shows an empty state; returning from the Property detail view returns to the Properties list.
  • The application distinguishes Instruction status from the relationship status and makes clear whether removed or sold relationships are included in displayed lists and counts.
  • An apartment or commercial Unit references exactly one enclosing Building for its active relationship period, and retrieving the Building shows that Unit through the inverse relationship.
  • Every Asset has an address or appropriate land/site location description and a geolocation; both are stored with available provenance and precision information.
  • An estate is recorded as a collection of land and buildings with a defined boundary; that boundary can be inspected with its source and is not represented as proof of title or cadastral boundaries.
  • A house, apartment, or factory can be represented as a building or unit at the appropriate level, without making the address the record identifier.
  • A site can be related to multiple parcels and buildings, and a building can be related to units, without implying legal ownership or boundaries.
  • A matter can reference the relevant Asset by stable identifier and assign a matter-specific role without changing the Asset's identity.
  • A Party can be associated with an Asset using an explicit, auditable relationship type and effective period.
  • Ending a relationship preserves its history, source, and attribution.
  • Self-links, invalid relationship types, and duplicate active relationships are rejected with actionable errors.
  • Changes to Asset details do not silently rewrite historic matter or transaction records.
  • Users can distinguish sourced or confirmed data from unverified descriptions where provenance is available.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Instruction is the shared finance-layer record for a mandate, engagement, or instruction. It represents the authorised business engagement between a client relationship and the legal entity that is party to the contract. It provides the common parent for WIP and billing records across service lines.

The Instruction connects to exactly one service-line record, selected by its service line. WIP records reference the Instruction rather than carrying their own service-line-specific parent lookups. The model therefore gives Finance a consistent parent while retaining service-line context in CRM.

This PRD uses the Core Shared Tables definition of kf_Instruction as the working baseline. The source material identifies it as authoritative, but also records unresolved conflicts that must be decided before implementation.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Finance needs a consistent record for the signed or otherwise authorised work that underlies WIP, billing, and revenue reporting. If each service line creates its own finance parent, WIP must understand each CRM table and reporting becomes fragmented. If the parent record does not distinguish the relationship-owning client from the contracting invoice entity, relationship reporting and billing can use the wrong organization.

The source model defines kf_Instruction, but its field set and automation requirements conflict with older definitions. This PRD turns the current Core model into product requirements while preserving those conflicts for approval.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Provide one stable finance parent for each service-line engagement.
  • Support Mandate, Engagement, and Instruction record types.
  • Identify both the Brand/Group relationship owner and the contracting Legal Entity.
  • Link the record to the correct service-line parent and enforce the single-parent rule.
  • Capture dates, ownership, status, and finance references needed to create and manage WIP.
  • Preserve auditable history and distinguish source CRM facts from finance-process data.
  • Support portfolio work without limiting an Instruction to one property.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Replacing service-line CRM records, their business-process flows, or deal lifecycle.
  • Tracking monthly WIP values, invoices, payments, probability, or period locks; those belong to kf_WIP.
  • Defining the full Account, Contact, Property, or service-line data models.
  • Performing KYC, AML screening, client verification, or compliance decisions.
  • Replacing the SharePoint WIP migration or Finance ERP integration plan.
  • Deciding unresolved source conflicts without the relevant business and data owners.

docs.title: Users and responsibilities
docs.text: User or system Need Case handler / service-line user Create and maintain an Instruction associated with the right client, legal entity, and service-line record. Finance user Use the Instruction as the parent for WIP and billing, with correct invoice entity and office context. Relationship / reporting user Attribute work to the Brand/Group client without confusing it with the invoice entity. Integrating systems Retrieve and update an Instruction using a stable identifier and an explicit schema. Operations / administrator Correct data, manage lifecycle status, and investigate changes through audit history.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Concept Meaning Instruction Shared finance-layer parent representing a mandate, engagement, or instruction. Instruction type Required classification: Mandate, Engagement, or Instruction. Client account Brand/Group account that owns the relationship and supports relationship reporting. Legal Entity account Contracting entity shown on the fee letter and invoice. Service-line parent The CRM record for the service line associated with this Instruction. Exactly one is populated, as selected by service line. WIP Finance child record(s) attached to the Instruction; WIP details are specified separately. Instruction-property link Association between an Instruction and one or more properties, using the universal kf_DealProperty junction in the source model.

docs.title: Create and activate an Instruction
docs.text:
1. A user or authorized system creates an Instruction with a type, service line, Brand/Group client, owning office, and start date.
  2. The system links the Instruction to the matching service-line parent and rejects a record with no parent, multiple parents, or a parent inconsistent with the selected service line.
  3. The user selects a Legal Entity account when known. For a Mandate, the source says the Legal Entity must exist by the Capital Markets Mandate stage (S3).
  4. The user records the signed date when the mandate is signed and sets the Instruction status to Active when work is authorized.
  5. Once the source-defined WIP entry conditions are met, a WIP record can reference this Instruction. The exact universal gate remains to be confirmed.

docs.title: Update or close an Instruction
docs.text:
1. An authorized user updates the Instruction's dates, accounts, service-line link, finance references, or status.
  2. The system validates conditional fields and records an auditable change.
  3. If an Instruction is withdrawn, any impact on its WIP children is handled by the approved cascade rule; the detailed rule is unresolved in the source.
  4. Historical WIP and process records remain interpretable after changes to the Instruction.

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text: Priority: Must is required for the initial usable release; Should is important but may follow; Could is a future enhancement.

docs.title: Identity and data
docs.text: ID Priority Requirement INS-1 Must Every Instruction has a stable unique identifier (kf_instructionid) and a system-generated reference (kf_name, proposed format INS-{SEQNUM:6}). INS-2 Must Every Instruction has exactly one required type: Mandate, Engagement, or Instruction. INS-3 Must Every Instruction has a required service line, client account, owning office, status, and start date. INS-4 Must kf_clientaccountid identifies the Brand/Group relationship owner and is not substituted for the legal invoice entity. INS-5 Must kf_legalentityaccountid, when populated, must reference an Account classified as Legal Entity. For a Mandate it must be present by the applicable mandate/billing gate; the exact universal timing requires approval. INS-6 Must The Instruction may reference a primary contact and a primary property. Neither is used as a substitute for the client account or service-line parent. INS-7 Must The record supports optional signed and end dates, expected revenue, termination reason, comments, and finance cross-reference fields defined by the approved schema. INS-8 Must A termination reason is required when the Instruction status is Withdrawn. INS-9 Must The system records creation and update timestamps and retains an auditable history of authorized changes. INS-10 Should Search and retrieval support the stable ID, generated reference, client, legal entity, service line, type, status, and available external finance references.

docs.title: Service-line relationship
docs.text:
ID Priority Requirement INS-11 Must Exactly one service-line parent lookup is populated on each Instruction, and the populated lookup must agree with kf_serviceline. INS-12 Must The service-line parent relationship is one-to-one from the service-line record's perspective. The Instruction is the shared finance parent; it does not replace the CRM parent. INS-13 Must A service-line parent cannot be silently changed to a different service line. An authorized correction must preserve audit history and any WIP references. INS-14 Must The initial schema and validation rules must use an approved list of service-line lookups and service-line values. The source lists 13 lookup targets while describing coverage as twelve service lines; this count and mapping must be reconciled before build. INS-15 Should The model supports rollout of additional service lines by adding an approved parent relationship without adding service-line-specific parent fields to kf_WIP.

The Core source lists these parent lookup targets: Deal, Engagement, Valuation Instruction, Lease, Property Mandate, Development Project, Debt Mandate, Building Survey, Workplace Assessment, Investor Mandate, Sales Instruction, Lettings Instruction, and ESG Assessment. The source notes that Residential Lettings has no target table defined, despite listing kf_lettingsinstructionid.

docs.title: Lifecycle and WIP relationship
docs.text:
ID Priority Requirement INS-16 Must The Instruction status supports Active, Completed, On Hold, and Withdrawn. Party/record status is distinct from legal standing of the client. INS-17 Must WIP records reference the Instruction through kf_WIP.kf_instructionid; the Instruction can have many WIP records. INS-18 Must WIP does not carry direct lookups to service-line CRM records. Service-line context is reached through the Instruction. INS-19 Must Changes to an Instruction do not silently rewrite historical WIP snapshots or process evidence. INS-20 Should An approved lifecycle rule defines whether Completed or Withdrawn Instructions can be edited, reactivated, or used to create additional WIP. INS-21 Should If a parent Instruction is withdrawn, the system applies the approved and idempotent disposition to its WIP children and records the outcome.

The requirement that WIP entry requires an Active Instruction and a populated kf_signeddate is an inference in the source material, not an approved baseline rule. It must not be enforced as a universal hard block until the business owner confirms it.

docs.title: Properties and portfolio work
docs.text: ID Priority Requirement INS-22 Must kf_propertyid supports an optional primary property reference. INS-23 Must An Instruction that covers multiple properties can associate them through the universal kf_DealProperty junction; a single property lookup must not be treated as the complete portfolio. INS-24 Should Property associations carry status and dates sufficient to preserve additions, removals, and historical context.

docs.title: Security, privacy, and operations
docs.text: ID Priority Requirement INS-25 Must Access to Instructions is scoped by the required owning office and follows approved role-based permissions. INS-26 Must Legal entity, registration, and finance references are exposed only to authorized callers and retained only for approved business purposes. INS-27 Must Create, update, status changes, and relationship corrections are attributable and auditable. INS-28 Should Integration and automation failures are visible to support users and do not leave a success-shaped partial Instruction.

docs.title: Data model baseline
docs.text:
The working Core Shared Tables schema includes:

  • kf_instructionid — GUID primary key.
  • kf_name — generated reference, INS-{SEQNUM:6}.
  • kf_instructiontype — Mandate / Engagement / Instruction.
  • kf_serviceline — global choice; selects the service-line parent lookup.
  • kf_clientaccountid — required Brand/Group Account.
  • kf_legalentityaccountid — Account filtered to Legal Entity.
  • kf_primarycontactid — optional Contact.
  • kf_propertyid — optional primary Property.
  • kf_owningoffice — required Business Unit.
  • kf_instructionstatus — Active / Completed / On Hold / Withdrawn.
  • kf_startdate — required; kf_signeddate and kf_enddate optional in the table definition.
  • kf_expectedrevenue — optional.
  • kf_terminationreason — conditionally required for Withdrawn.
  • kf_comments — optional multi-line text.
  • kf_fin_localsystemref, kf_fin_localsystemname, and kf_fin_projectid — finance-system references.
  • One service-line-specific parent lookup, as selected by service line.

The full field-level contract, option values, validation timing, and localization rules require approval before API or Dataverse implementation.

docs.title: Integrations and dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Instruction use Account Brand/Group client and filtered Legal Entity invoice account. Contact Optional primary contact. Business Unit Required owning office; supports security scope and downstream finance defaults. Service-line CRM tables Exactly one parent relationship selected by service line. Capital Markets is the initial live pipeline in the source rollout. Property / kf_DealProperty Optional primary property and multi-property portfolio association. kf_WIP One Instruction to many WIP records; WIP retrieves service-line context through Instruction. Finance / ERP Local system name, local system reference, and finance project ID are carried for current/manual or future integrated use. ERP automation is deferred to Phase 7 in the source rollout.

docs.title: Scope and rollout
docs.text:
• Foundation / Phase 0: build the shared Instruction schema and its core Account, Business Unit, and property relationships, subject to confirmation of activation timing. The source marks Instruction as MVP but omits it from the explicit activation tables.
  • Phase 1: support Paris Capital Markets and its Deal relationship; make the Instruction usable as the parent for WIP and support the SharePoint WIP cutover.
  • Later phases: activate other service-line parent lookups as their CRM solutions and workflows become available.
  • Phase 7: enable the consolidated Finance ERP integration. Until then, source material indicates that finance references may be maintained manually.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
1. A user can create and retrieve an Instruction using its stable ID and generated reference.
  2. Required fields, type/status values, Legal Entity filtering, and conditional termination reason are validated consistently through supported interfaces.
  3. A saved Instruction has exactly one service-line parent matching its service line, using the approved relationship map.
  4. Finance users can distinguish the Brand/Group relationship owner from the Legal Entity used for contracting and invoicing.
  5. An Instruction can have multiple WIP children, and each WIP record reaches service-line context only through the Instruction.
  6. Portfolio property associations can be represented without losing the primary property reference.
  7. Authorized edits and lifecycle changes are auditable; previous process/WIP records remain interpretable.
  8. The agreed MVP activation phase, WIP-entry gate, withdrawal cascade, and source schema are documented and approved before production release.

docs.title: Open decisions and source conflicts
docs.text:
These are decisions, not assumptions:

  1. Schema version: The Core Shared Tables definition is treated as authoritative, but an older definition includes kf_transactiontype, kf_sector, kf_negotiatorid, and kf_currency, while the Core definition omits them. WIP's classification-population requirements rely on some of this context. Confirm the final Instruction fields and each WIP field's authoritative source.
  2. Parent mapping and count: The source says twelve service lines but lists thirteen parent lookups. It also lists a Lettings lookup without a target table. Approve the actual service-line values, lookup targets, and rollout mapping.
  3. Status: Confirm the Core statuses (Active / Completed / On Hold / Withdrawn) and their transitions, including whether reactivation is allowed.
  4. Mandate gates: Confirm whether an Active status and signed date are hard requirements for WIP creation, and when the Legal Entity must be present outside the described Capital Markets S3 gate.
  5. Withdrawal cascade: Confirm whether withdrawal sets all child WIP records to Lost, what happens to billed or paid records, and how the cascade is audited.
  6. Activation phase: Instruction is marked MVP but omitted from the explicit Phase 0/1 activation table. Confirm the activation phase and update the programme list.
  7. Finance references: Confirm the source of local system defaults, whether the local reference belongs on Instruction or WIP, and when kf_fin_projectid is populated.
  8. Historical data: Decide whether full field-level history, attributed audit events, or process-specific snapshots are required for client, legal entity, parent, and property relationship changes.
  9. Concurrency and uniqueness: Confirm whether a service-line parent can have only one Instruction and how duplicates are handled during migration and create.
  10. Term definitions: Confirm whether Mandate / Engagement / Instruction are mutually exclusive business record types or labels that have different lifecycle and commercial requirements.

docs.title: Party application architecture
docs.text: The Party POC is a browser-native static Party catalogue with an optional Companies House proxy. The canonical architecture diagram is architecture.puml and uses the PlantUML ArchiMate library.

docs.title: Current architecture
docs.text:
